rule.title: The Four Pillars of Unit Test Quality
rule.statement: Every unit test must maximize Protection Against Regressions, Resistance to Refactoring, Fast Feedback, and Maintainability.
rule.rationale: A test suite that scores poorly on Resistance to Refactoring generates False Positives whenever code is restructured, causing developers to abandon testing.
rule.implementation_guidance: Test observable behaviors rather than internal implementation details. If refactoring without changing behavior breaks tests, rewrite the tests.

forbidden.example: expect(service['privateStep2']).toHaveBeenCalled(); // Fragile test bound to implementation detail

source.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
source.chapter: Chapter 4: The Four Pillars of a Good Unit Test
source.evidence_quote: A good unit test has four foundational attributes: protection against regressions, resistance to refactoring, fast feedback, and maintainability. Resistance to refactoring is non-negotiable.

rule.title: Standardized Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) Test Structure
rule.statement: Every test case must follow the Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) pattern with clearly separated phases, containing only a single Act invocation.
rule.rationale: Interweaving setup, multiple acts, and repeated assertions turns tests into confusing multi-step scripts, making it difficult to pinpoint failure causes.
rule.implementation_guidance: Structure each test with 3 distinct comment blocks or visual whitespace: // Arrange, // Act, // Assert.

forbidden.example: const u = makeUser(); auth(u); u.name = 'x'; update(u); expect(u).toBe(...); delete(u); expect(u).toBeNull();

source.book_title: Unit Testing Principles, Practices, and Patterns
source.chapter: Chapter 3: The Anatomy of a Unit Test
source.evidence_quote: The AAA pattern provides a uniform structure across all tests in a test suite. It splits a test into three sections: Arrange, Act, and Assert.
